nodes.label: ADR 0129: Refresh the code map's docs in every session
nodes.rationale: Docs in the graph must always be kept current. A session that orients with graphify would miss decisions taken the session before if the docs aren't refreshed. Batch processing on Haiku (cheapest model) costs about 73k tokens for 7 docs.

nodes.label: scripts/graph_docs.py: docs refresh tool
nodes.rationale: Prepare: lists changed docs, writes prompts per batch of 15 (.docs_NN.md). Finish: mends subagent output, fills semantic cache, updates code part, merges, prunes, clusters, publishes to graphify branch.

nodes.label: Code map docs batch refresh process
nodes.rationale: Every session that changes docs refreshes them before commit: prepare lists docs, one subagent per batch reads and writes JSON, finish merges output and publishes. Batches of 15 on Haiku model for efficiency. Docs with failed batch stay unstamped and retry.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore: exclude vault/log/
nodes.rationale: Changelog, handoff, and archive left out of graph; changelog is long and read every session anyway.

nodes.label: Semantic cache for doc refresh
nodes.rationale: Filled during finish step; docs seen before by content come from cache to reduce redundant processing.

nodes.label: graph.html: interactive view on website
nodes.rationale: Published with the graph on graphify branch; site's deploy copies it. Allows browsing without running anything locally.

nodes.label: Cost efficiency: batch refresh on Haiku
nodes.rationale: Measured ~73k tokens for 7 docs; most cost is subagent startup, not docs. Batching on Haiku (cheapest model) reduces per-session cost vs 60 KB skill overhead.
